headline: VRR uses verification feedback to expand candidate search, with mixed reported benchmark results
summary: Tomihari and Ichikawa introduce Verify–Repair–Reselect (VRR), which feeds verifier diagnostics back into generation: after ranking an initial pool, it retains the winner, conditionally creates repairs of the winner and runner-up plus a new-approach candidate, filters invalid/duplicate outputs and reselects under the original criteria. Across two models and eight code/reasoning benchmarks, the authors report VRR beats fixed-pool LAV selection in 9 of 16 settings. Table 1 includes improvements as well as null and negative cells. On LiveCodeBench, the authors report recovery on some problems where all initial candidates were incorrect. These are paper-reported results using the same model for generation, verification and repair; matched total-inference-budget comparison with best-of-N and independent reproduction remain open.
